# FHIR Billing Core

- **Purpose:** Jurisdiction-neutral FHIR R4 billing contracts and their reference evaluator.
- **Product:** cognovis FHIR implementation guides (`fhir`), module Implementation Guides
- **Role:** building-block
- **Audience:** partners
- **Customer:** none

- **Used by:** `cognovis/fhir-billing-ch`, `cognovis/fhir-billing-de`

<!-- cognovis-map:end -->

Jurisdiction-neutral FHIR R4 contracts for deterministic medical billing rules
and their reference evaluator.

- Package: `de.cognovis.fhir.billing.core`
- Canonical: `https://fhir.cognovis.de/billing-core`
- FHIR version: R4 (`4.0.1`)
- License: Apache-2.0 for Cognovis-authored material

FHIR Billing Core owns every evaluator-supported rule type, including its
typed inputs, calculation algorithm, ordering, precision, result, and
diagnostic semantics. A rule type belongs here even when its first known use is
limited to one jurisdiction. Neither Billing Core nor a country package ships
actual rules or rule values (product-owner decision, 2026-10-07): rule
instances, legal and contractual values and their effective periods are
imported content that the customer-local reference-data adapter writes at
runtime or an external rule-set author supplies. Country packages own regimes,
mappings, terminology and tariff bindings, and source-publication decisions.
Billing Core tests its rule code with synthetic rule sets and synthetic code
systems only.

The engine assumes that an admitted catalog edition and rule set are already
loaded. Billing Core uses base R4 resources rather than custom resource profiles:
catalog definitions are `ChargeItemDefinition`; catalog editions, configured
rules, and aggregated rule sets are `Library`; publication evidence is
`Provenance`; and evaluator fixtures are `Parameters`. Identifier systems,
FHIR-native `Library.type`, exact `canonical|version` relationships,
`application/json` Library attachments, and versioned JSON payloads distinguish
those artifacts. A
catalog edition persists exact definition and rule-set versions for one
applicability period. The SDK `BillingSnapshot` is only the transient,
version-bound evaluation read set and is not another stored catalog.

The edition manifest carries catalog scope, publication period, and normalized
source records. The source-set digest is SHA-256 over canonical JSON after a
deterministic sort. Completeness, compatibility, availability, and digest match
are derived by the SDK. Admission comes only from the tenant's admission records
in FHIR (described in the Billing SDK guide (`fhir-foundation/packages/fhir-billing-sdk/docs/guide.md` in the cognovis Health Platform repository)): `Provenance` resources a
producer writes when it imports and admits an edition, binding the exact
canonical, version, digest and source-set digest of each admitted artifact for
one tenant. The SDK reads nothing but FHIR and knows no producer. There is no
allow-all default.

Source acquisition, licensing, tenant selection, persistence, and
country-specific adapters are outside this repository. Catalog and rule
artifacts are master data; this package does not create `ChargeItem` movement
records.

The repository contains one FHIR R4 implementation guide and three TypeScript
packages, published on `npm.cognovis.de` and readable without credentials. None
of them depends on a cognovis SDK; CI refuses a manifest that declares one
(`npm run check:engine-manifests`):

- `@cognovis/fhir-billing-types` exposes native-carrier constants, payload
  schemas, base R4 resource shapes, and runtime types.
- `@cognovis/fhir-billing-rules` owns payload-v2, admission, migration constants,
  the generic rule-class registry, and the shared native `Library` codec.
- `@cognovis/fhir-billing-engine` compiles admitted immutable rule sets and
  evaluates cases with exact-decimal precision and priority-then-id ordering. It
  also evaluates a rule set on synthetic cases in standalone mode and compares
  the records of two engines. See
  [Standalone evaluation and comparison](#standalone-evaluation-and-comparison).

`@cognovis/fhir-billing-sdk`, which evaluates authoritative FHIR billing data
against these packages, is not part of this repository. Since 0.37.1 it is
maintained and published from the cognovis Health Platform under its existing
npm name; its documentation is the Billing SDK guide (`fhir-foundation/packages/fhir-billing-sdk/docs/guide.md` in the cognovis Health Platform repository). Mentions of "the SDK" below
describe that consumer of the engine contract.

## Standalone evaluation and comparison

A rule-set author can evaluate one rule set on synthetic cases without MIRA, a
FHIR server, a catalog edition or a tenant, and diff the result against another
engine. The library entry point is `evaluateConformanceCases({ ruleSet, cases })`
in `@cognovis/fhir-billing-engine` (IO-free); the command-line tool
`fhir-billing-check` is a `bin` of `@cognovis/fhir-billing-sdk` and reads files
around the same function. This typed-case path does not load
`@cognovis/fhir-sdk`; only the SDK's `evaluate --bundle` does.

```sh
npx fhir-billing-check evaluate --rule-set rule-set.json --cases cases.jsonl > ours.jsonl
npx fhir-billing-check compare ours.jsonl theirs.jsonl
```

Inputs:

- The rule set is either a rule-set `Library` carrier or a bare `BillingRuleSet`
  payload (`schemaVersion`, `semanticMajor`, `id`, `rules`). A Library is decoded
  with `decodeBillingLibrary` and must be artifact-kind `rule-set`; its declared
  digest must match the payload. A bare payload is decoded by the same strict
  payload decoder the Library codec uses (`decodeBillingRuleSet`: exactly
  these four top-level keys, only the known rule keys, a non-empty rule `id` and
  `class`), and its digest is computed as the SDK computes it
  (`billingRulePayloadDigest({ schemaVersion: 2, rules })`). A malformed rule set, a digest mismatch, another Library kind, or an unsupported payload
  schema or semantic major throws `BillingInputError` before any record; the
  command exits 2 and prints nothing on stdout.
- Cases are `BillingCase` objects, as a JSON array (when the whole file parses as
  one JSON array) or otherwise as JSON Lines (blank lines ignored), so a JSON
  Lines file whose first line is `[]` reads that line as one malformed case. Each
  case supplies its own prices, facts, counting windows and contracts. A case
  line carries a `unitPrice` or, for an unknown amount, `unitPriceUnknown: true`
  (exactly one of them); a line with neither is a malformed case. A line that
  is not valid JSON is an input error of the file (exit 2), not a malformed case.
  Case ids must be unique, including the `#<n>` fallback ids: a duplicate is an
  input error of the whole run (`BillingInputError`, exit 2, nothing on stdout).
- Every input file of `evaluate` and `compare` is UTF-8; a leading byte order
  mark is ignored.

Standalone admission: the given rule set is its own admitted, complete,
entitled edition with its own digest, and the catalog edition is the
placeholder `standalone`. No tenant entitlement or catalog membership is
checked. A rule-set Library's `effectivePeriod` still applies: a case dated
before its start or after its end is `unavailable` with `EDITION_UNAVAILABLE` or
`EDITION_EXPIRED`. Every record carries `mode: "standalone"`, so it can never be
taken for an admitted production verdict of the Billing SDK.

Each case yields one `fhir-billing-conformance/1` record, in input order,
serialized as canonical JSON (`canonicalizeJson`, sorted keys), one per line.
Two runs on the same inputs are byte-identical.

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `format` | `fhir-billing-conformance/1` |
| `mode` | `standalone` |
| `caseId` | the case `id`, or `#<1-based position>` when it has none |
| `decision` | `allow`, `block` or `unavailable`, from the engine outcome `accepted`, `rejected` or `needs-review` (as the SDK maps it) |
| `ruleSet` | `id` and payload `digest`; `canonical` (Library.url) and `version` only for a Library; `publisher` only for a Library that names one (see [Rule provenance and publisher](#rule-provenance-and-publisher)) |
| `engineVersion` | the Billing Core version |
| `ignoredRuleIds` | sorted ids of rules the engine skipped because their class is unsupported and `mustUnderstand` is `false`; omitted when there are none |
| `advisories` | engine advisories, omitted when there are none |
| `findings` | every axis reason: `code`, `ruleId`, `lineId`, `effect` (`reject` or `needs-review`), `details`, `resolution` when the reason has one (see [Reason resolutions](#reason-resolutions)), and `sources` and `evidenceLevel` when the producing rule has provenance |

Findings are sorted by `ruleId`, then `lineId`, then `code`, then the canonical
JSON of `details` (a missing value sorts first), whatever the rule priority or
line order. Withheld admission reasons carry effect `needs-review`. A case the
engine cannot read (not an object, a wrong shape of any required or optional
field, or a `BillingInputError` such as a negative quantity) yields `decision: "unavailable"` with one finding
`{ code: "BILLING_INPUT_INVALID", effect: "needs-review", details: { message } }`
(`fhir-billing-check` prints it without `message`), and the run
continues with the next case. `BILLING_INPUT_INVALID` belongs to the
record format only; it is not a `BillingReasonCode`.

`compareConformanceRecords(left, right)` and `fhir-billing-check compare <left>
<right>` key both record lists by `caseId`; a duplicate `caseId` on one side is an
input error. A case is reported when the decisions differ or the sets of blocking
`(lineId, ruleId)` pairs differ, where a blocking pair is a finding with effect
`reject`. Reason codes, review findings, finding order, `resolution`, `sources`, `evidenceLevel`, the
rule-set `publisher` and unknown fields are not compared, so records of another engine are accepted when they carry `caseId`,
`decision` and `findings` whose entries have a string `code` and an `effect` of
`reject` or `needs-review` (both required); `ruleId` and `lineId` are optional
strings, and `null` counts as absent. The same file-format rule and byte order
mark handling as for `evaluate` cases apply. The output
holds only the differences, as canonical JSON Lines sorted by `caseId`:
`{ kind: "disagree", caseId, differs, left, right }`, `{ kind: "left-only", caseId,
left }` or `{ kind: "right-only", caseId, right }`, where each side is
`{ decision, blocking }`.

A counting-scoped `quantity-limit` (one with `countingScope`) reports every
selected line in the counting window once the window total exceeds the maximum,
not only the line that crosses it. A foreign engine that flags only the excess
line therefore shows a `blocking` difference on that case even when both decide
`block`; map such a rule onto the whole window, or expect that difference.

The standalone evaluator only knows Core rule classes. When the other engine's
rules come from a translator (for example, the reference-data adapter works
with internal classes such as `factor-bound` and maps them to
`bounded-multiplier` when it writes carriers), evaluate and compare against the
published Core carrier form of those rules, not the translator's internal form.

| Exit code | `evaluate` | `compare` |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | records printed | every case agrees |
| 1 | not used | at least one difference |
| 2 | usage or input error, nothing on stdout | usage or input error, nothing on stdout |


## Rule provenance and publisher

Rule sets for real fee schedules and contract tariffs are imported content that
third parties maintain; Billing Core ships no real rules. Core gives such a rule
set two places to say where it comes from and who answers for it.

A rule may carry `provenance` (payload schema 2, type `BillingRuleProvenance`):

```json
{
  "sources": [
    { "kind": "fee-schedule", "citation": "Synthetic dental fee schedule 2026, section 2" },
    {
      "kind": "court-decision",
      "citation": "Synthetic Regional Court, file 1 S 23/26, decision of 2026-03-12",
      "uri": "https://example.invalid/decisions/1-s-23-26",
      "codes": ["SD-0010"]
    }
  ],
  "evidenceLevel": { "system": "https://example.invalid/CodeSystem/synthetic-evidence-level", "code": "binding" },
  "note": "Optional free text."
}
```

- `sources` is a non-empty list of `BillingRuleSource`: `kind` is one of
  `BILLING_RULE_SOURCE_KINDS` (`statute`, `fee-schedule`, `contract`,
  `court-decision`, `authority-statement`, `commentary`, `author-assessment`),
  `citation` is non-empty text (a `court-decision` names court, file number and
  decision date there), `uri` is optional, and `codes` optionally lists the
  unique fee numbers the source concerns.
- `evidenceLevel` is a `Coding` (`system` and `code` required, `display` and
  `version` optional). The rule-set author chooses the system and its scale;
  Core defines no evidence-level scale and never interprets the code.
- `note` is optional non-empty text.

`defineBillingRuleSet`, `decodeBillingRuleSet` and the Library codec refuse an
unknown top-level rule key (so a misspelled `provenence` fails on the typed API
too), an unknown key in `provenance`, a source or the evidence level, an empty `sources`
list, an unknown `kind`, an empty `citation`, a malformed `evidenceLevel` and
blank or duplicate `codes` with a `BillingInputError` naming the rule id. Validity per
rule stays `effectiveStart` and `effectiveEnd`; the rule-set Library's
`effectivePeriod` bounds the whole rule set. The rule-set digest
(`billingRulePayloadDigest({ schemaVersion: 2, rules })`) covers provenance, so a
changed citation is a new rule-set version.

Provenance never changes evaluation: decisions, reason codes, `details`,
`resolution` and reason order are the same with and without it. Every reason a
rule with provenance produces carries that rule's `sources` and `evidenceLevel`,
as the rule states them: on the engine's `BillingReason`, the SDK's
`BillingDecisionReason`, and the findings of typed and bundle conformance
records. A rule without provenance yields reasons without either field, and
reasons without a rule (`ELIGIBLE`, admission reasons, selection reasons) never
carry them.

A rule-set Library names its publisher, the party that maintains the rule set
and is responsible for it, in `Library.publisher`, and may carry
`Library.contact` (FHIR `ContactDetail` entries with `name` and `telecom`).
The publisher is carrier metadata outside the payload digest: re-wrapping the
same payload in a Library that names another publisher keeps the digest. Only an
admission record attests it: the record binds a rule set's `publisher` (absent
when the Library names none), and a rule set is admitted only under the
publisher its record binds. `bundleAdmissionRecords` binds the publisher of the
supplied Library. The standalone typed path has no admission and reports the
publisher as the Library declares it.
`buildBillingLibrary` requires a non-empty `publisher` for kind `rule-set`, as it
does for a catalog edition. `decodeBillingLibrary` still reads a rule-set Library
without `publisher`, because rule sets published before 0.17.0 (for example the
reference-data adapter's) carry none; such a rule set decodes and evaluates as
before, and its records name no publisher. The decoded value exposes `publisher`
and `contact` when present. The conformance record's `ruleSet` (and, in a bundle
record, each `ruleSets` entry) names the `publisher` of its Library;
`compareConformanceRecords` ignores it. A bundle record names it only for a rule
set an admission record of the tenant admitted in the evaluation that returned
the result (`bundleConformanceRecord` of a result the SDK did not return, for
example a copy, names none): an edition's rule set its admission record does not
bind, or one the evaluation stopped before admitting, has no `publisher` in the record, and a
decisive gate overlay's `ruleSet.publisher` is its verdict's attested publisher
or absent. Contract rule sets are not named in a record.

## Contract-bound catalog editions

Since 0.41.0 a native catalog edition can be bound to the Contracts whose own
tariff it is, for example one HZV price list per HZV contract
(cognovis/fhir-billing-core#127,
[ADR-005](docs/adr/ADR-005-contract-bound-catalog-editions.md)). Its manifest
names the Contract canonicals in `contracts` (each a `Contract.url` or
`Contract.instantiatesUri`, optionally `|version`, unique), and the Library
carries one `depends-on` related artifact per Contract and no other.
`buildBillingLibrary` writes the links from the manifest; a `depends-on` link is
no build input. Each catalog definition entry of a bound edition also carries
the definition's billed coding (`system|code`) in the extension
`BILLING_CATALOG_DEFINITION_CODING_EXTENSION`
(`https://fhir.cognovis.de/billing-core/extension/catalog-definition-coding`),
written by the builder from `catalogDefinitions` (each with exactly one coding).
A bound edition is built from its whole inventory: every member must be a given
catalog definition, the given `ruleSet` Library or one of the given
`configuredRules`; any other member is refused.
The member-set digest covers the sorted Contracts and each entry's coding as
`{ scheme: 2, members, contracts }`, so the admission record binds the Contract
assignment and the codings the edition holds. An unbound edition has no
`contracts` and no entry codings, and keeps its digest. `decodeBillingLibrary`
refuses an edition whose `depends-on` links are not exactly its manifest's
Contracts, including one bound by only one of the two. Selecting a bound edition
for a case is the Billing SDK's task (ADR-005).

## Engine contract

The public result is tri-state: `accepted`, `rejected`, or `needs-review`.
Malformed inputs throw `BillingInputError`; unusable editions and unknown
must-understand rules produce `needs-review` instead of being accepted.
Admission is fail-closed: both edition digests must be explicitly verified and
the admitted rule-set edition must equal the rule-set id. An edition of
completeness `complete` or `partial` is admitted; only completeness `unknown`
withholds it with `ADMISSION_INCOMPLETE` (see
partial catalog editions in the Billing SDK guide (`fhir-foundation/packages/fhir-billing-sdk/docs/guide.md` in the cognovis Health Platform repository)). Rules declare a
`reject` or `needs-review` effect, and effective periods are applied against the
case date. Exact monetary arithmetic accepts at most two fractional digits and
requires non-negative integer quantities; unsupported fractional quantities are
typed input errors rather than silently rounded values.

Every rule selects its lines through `parameters.selector`, a non-empty `codes`
list with an optional `system`. Codes match literally, except that `"*"` as the
only entry of `codes` selects every line code within the optional `system`.
Without a `system`, `"*"` selects the lines of every code system in the case;
regime scoping comes from the rule set composition or from `selector.system`.
Mixing `"*"` with other codes is ambiguous and a `BillingInputError`. The
`excluded` selector of `mutual-exclusion` and the `required` selector of
`companion-required` stay literal; `"*"` there is also a `BillingInputError`.
The `mutual-exclusion` presence check includes the selected line itself, as it
already does for overlapping literal selectors, so a `"*"` primary selector with
`excluded` code X rejects every case that contains X.

Rules may additionally declare required facts, counting scopes, fact-driven
exceptions, modifier exceptions, multiplier thresholds, and agreement override
evidence. Cases represent fact availability explicitly and identify the lines in
each counting window. A line may carry its own `facts`: the line-scoped classes
(`patient-attribute-constraint`, `setting-constraint`,
`prior-authorization-required`, `diagnosis-requirement`,
`provider-eligibility`, `accompanying-information-required`) then decide that
line alone on its values in place of the case facts, for the class fact and for
the rule's `requiredFacts` and `exceptWhen`, and a finding without a line names
it. A line carrying `information` gives
`accompanying-information-required` its information alone: a name it lacks is
`not-supplied` for that line. Line facts and information are validated like
case facts; a case without them evaluates exactly as before. A bounded-multiplier rule requires an actual multiplier;
missing facts, windows, multipliers, or conditional agreement evidence yield
typed `needs-review` reasons.

### Reason resolutions

A block reason may carry `resolution: { action, codes }`, a typed list of the
codings that would resolve it, beside the string-valued `details`. Each code has
`code`, `system` when the rule or the case names one, `lineId` when it is a line
of the case, and `qualifiers` when it is an admissible member that declares
qualifiers. `add-one-of` means any one of `codes` satisfies the rule, with one of
the listed values for every listed qualifier; `remove` means the listed present
codes caused, or may have caused, the block. Codes are de-duplicated by `system`,
`code`, `lineId` and `qualifiers`; the first occurrence keeps its position.

| Reason | `action` | `codes` |
|---|---|---|
| `COMPANION_CODE_REQUIRED` | `add-one-of` | the rule's `required` codes, with its `system` when given, in configured order |
| `DIAGNOSIS_NOT_SATISFIED`, polarity `include` | `add-one-of` | the predicate's admissible `valueIn` codes, with its `system` when given and each member's qualifier alternation when it declares one |
| `DIAGNOSIS_NOT_SATISFIED`, polarity `exclude` | `remove` | every present case entry with an admissible code that did not definitively mismatch (it matched, or it lacks the system or a qualifier the predicate needs), with code and system as supplied, in supplied order |
| `PROCEDURE_FINDING_NOT_SATISFIED` | as `DIAGNOSIS_NOT_SATISFIED` | as `DIAGNOSIS_NOT_SATISFIED` |
| `MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE_CODE_PRESENT` | `remove` | exactly the reason's own line when it matches the `excluded` selector itself; otherwise every other present line matching `excluded`, each with its `lineId` and system, in line order |

On `MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE_CODE_PRESENT`, the presence check includes the reason's
own line. With an overlapping or `"*"` selector the own line can match
`excluded` itself; then a code whose `lineId` equals the reason's own `lineId` is
the whole resolution, because removing that line is the only fix that resolves
the reason. Applying the listed removals and evaluating again never yields this
reason for this line.

Only a finding with effect `reject` carries a resolution. A rule configured with
effect `needs-review` and every indeterminate reason carry none, and no other
reason does, including multiplier, quantity and admission reasons. A resolution informs a UI that
offers the fix; it never changes an outcome, a reason code, the reason order or
`details`, and the engine neither proposes, ranks nor writes a fix. The SDK's
`BillingDecisionReason` and the standalone conformance findings carry it
unchanged; `compareConformanceRecords` ignores it. The types
`BillingReasonResolution` and `BillingResolutionCode` are exported from the
types, engine and SDK packages.

Consumers migrating from 0.6.3 should stop writing Billing Core
`meta.profile` values and extension stacks. Write the base resources and native
discriminators described above. The SDK retains isolated read compatibility for
legacy catalog-edition `_profile` discovery and legacy admission extensions;
new artifacts must use the native carrier codec and admission records.
`migration/canonical-map.json` records each removed identity and its replacement
convention.

`minimum-evidence-count` is the neutral count rule for one or more named
numeric evidence facts. Each source has a positive safe-integer credit and may
cap its own credited contribution. Known absence contributes zero; unavailable
facts yield `needs-review`; malformed values and unsafe arithmetic are typed
input errors. The rule semantic major is 4, while payload schema 2 and its
canonical digest remain unchanged.

Payload-v2 digests use UTF-8 canonical JSON: object keys are sorted by JavaScript
code-unit order, object properties with `undefined` values are omitted, array
`undefined` values become `null`, array order is retained, and primitives use
`JSON.stringify` number and string forms. The pinned cross-repository vector in
`fixtures/payload-v2-digest.json` is the compatibility authority. Value-limit
rules compare pre-multiplier unit price times integer quantity; multiplier
constraints are expressed by the separate bounded-multiplier rule class.

A `BillingLine` carries exactly one of `unitPrice` and `unitPriceUnknown: true`;
both or neither is a `BillingInputError`. `unitPriceUnknown` means the amount is
unknown, not zero: a `value-limit` gives a selected line with it the
`needs-review` reason `UNIT_PRICE_UNAVAILABLE` and compares every other line as
before. `resolveCatalogUnitPrices` fills a line with a numeric-zero placeholder
or the marker from the `CatalogPriceTable`: an entry with `unitPrice` prices it
in the table `currency`, an entry with `unitPriceUnknown: true` (a points-only
definition) leaves it unknown. A table entry carries exactly one of the two, and
`currency` may be absent only when no entry has a `unitPrice`.

## Build and verification

The engine packages declare no dependency or peer dependency on any cognovis
SDK and carry Apache-2.0; `scripts/engine-manifest-guard.mjs`
(`npm run check:engine-manifests`) enforces it in `npm test`, in
`.github/workflows/validate.yml` and before packing in the release workflow.
The packed portability check installs the three archives offline into an empty
consumer, refuses any further cognovis package in its tree, typechecks the
public types and proves evaluator decisions and a refusal in Node and Bun. The
release workflow proves the exact archive set it publishes.

Run `npm install`, then `npm run verify`. The verification builds the TypeScript
packages, exercises the neutral and synthetic German/Swiss fixtures through the
same engine, regenerates Core type metadata from the existing IG build output,
and scans exact npm tarballs for dependency, license, notice, and
prohibited-content violations.

Development needs the latest released Bun and the latest Node LTS (`.nvmrc`).
`tsc` compiles and type-checks; `bun test` runs the compiled suites, and the
repository's own helpers run on Bun. Node remains where something else requires
it:

- npm: the `package-lock.json` workspaces, `npm ci`, `npm pack` and the
  registry publish.
- `scripts/verify-packed-portability.mjs` runs on `node`, because it proves the
  packed units for a Node consumer through `process.execPath` (and for a Bun
  consumer through `bun`).

The FHIR IG build (SUSHI plus IG Publisher) runs only through
`npm run fhir:publisher` (`cognovis-fhir ig build`); Jekyll must be available on
`PATH`. Run it before `npm run verify`: the build records the fingerprint of
`sushi-config.yaml` and `input/fsh` in `fsh-generated/`, and the type
generation and release checks refuse a missing or stale `fsh-generated/`
instead of regenerating metadata from outdated resources. The tracked
pipeline forces offline terminology resolution, rejects the prohibited remote
host, and fails on Publisher QA errors. FHIR publication remains outside this
repository workflow. npm packages are published
to `https://npm.cognovis.de` with `publishConfig.access` `public` by the GitHub
Actions release workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`), which runs on a
pushed `v<version>` tag and needs the repository secrets `NPM_TOKEN` (publish
token for `npm.cognovis.de`) and `PACKAGE_REGISTRY_READ_TOKEN` (installs
`ccore`). The workflow's `build` job tests, packs and runs the packed consumers
without any secret; its `publish` job holds both secrets, runs no repository or
dependency code, and publishes only archives whose sha256 equals the one `build`
recorded at packing. Pull requests and pushes to `main` run
`.github/workflows/validate.yml`.
Each package declares a fresh per-version `publishConfig.tag`. The release
workflow passes that tag explicitly, verifies all existing npm pointers remain
unchanged, and creates the GitHub release with `--latest=false`, verifying the
previous latest release is preserved. An npm release does not publish an IG.
`bun scripts/verify-release.mjs --published` verifies authenticated metadata,
tarball retrieval, and anonymous HTTP 200 for those public units.
